title: Block motif — four round
subtitle: A solid square worked in the round with four rounds of treble clusters and chain corners
excerpt: Four rounds from the magic ring produce a 9 cm square block with solid treble-cluster sides and chain-2 corners. The construction is the same as the granny square but the sides stay solid — no side chain spaces — giving a tighter, denser fabric with a clear square outline.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 1 (1885), solid square block chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886).
heroPrompt: A four-round solid block crochet motif in warm cream DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Dense treble sides with chain-2 corners, 9 cm square.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished block measures 9 × 9 cm in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Block motif — four round
chartDefinition.caption: Four rounds from the magic ring. Chain-2 corner spaces; no chain-1 side spaces — trebles fill the sides solidly.

glossaryTerms.definition: A block motif side where trebles are worked directly into the previous round without a separating chain-1 space, giving a denser fabric than the traditional granny square construction.

content.text: The four-round block motif works the same corner chain-2 structure as the granny square but omits the side chain-1 spaces, packing trebles into the sides to give
. Four rounds give a 9 cm square with a clear corner definition and a body that does not stretch out of shape when worn.
Use this block where the granny square would be too open — cushion covers, bag panels, and hat brim tiles work well. Join on any side with whip stitch or slip stitch.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 10 g of DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: Magic ring. Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 2 tr into ring. *Ch 2, 3 tr into ring.* Rep 3 more times. Ch 2. Sl st to top of beg ch-3. Close ring. (12 tr, 4 ch-2 corners.)

Sl st to first ch-2 corner sp. Ch 3. Into same corner sp: 2 tr, ch 2, 3 tr. *Tr into each tr across the side (all previous-round side trebles, no skipping). Into next ch-2 corner sp: 3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr.* Rep from * around. Sl st to top of beg ch-3 to join. (Side treble count: Rnd 2 = 3 per side; Rnd 3 = 6 per side; Rnd 4 = 9 per side.)
For a larger version of the same construction, work the six-round block. Or try the bavarian crochet square for a post-stitch alternative to the solid block.
